# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual for defusing the bomb:
1. Cut the yellow wire.
2. Press the key that wears 2.
3. Cut the orange wire.
4. Press the key that wears 7.
All strictly in that order.

This is Turn 1, and I go first in the speaking order (Mute, Blind, Deaf). Because I cannot speak, I can only communicate to Deaf via gestures. However, Deaf cannot hear, Blind cannot see gestures, and no convention or meaning has been established yet for any signs. Deaf has not yet seen or described the bomb's layout, nor established how they want me to signal choices to them.

Deaf can speak out loud to Blind and me once Deaf observes the bomb. Therefore, I must wait for Blind and Deaf to take their turns, describe what they perceive, and establish a common signaling convention.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind reporting bomb state: Modules present: DISPLAY, LIGHT, STRIP, KEYPAD, WIRES. STRIP has 3 engraved symbols: Symbol 1 is a spiral or swirl curving inward; Symbol 2 is the exact same inward spiral or swirl; Symbol 3 is five dots arranged in an X or quincunx pattern like the five face of a gaming die. KEYPAD has 4 keys: slot 1 is 2, slot 2 is 3, slot 3 is 7, slot 4 is 1. It requires 2 digits, currently entered nothing. WIRES has 6 wire positions, numbered 1 to 6. DISPLAY and LIGHT are present but unknown to me. My possible actions are act(op='press', slot=N) for N 1 to 4, and act(op='cut', position=N) for N 1 to 6.
Deaf says: Bomb state: DISPLAY shows 6. LIGHT is green. STRIP is painted red, blue, yellow. KEYPAD buttons are 1:2, 2:3, 3:7, 4:1, requires 2 digits, currently entered nothing. WIRES 1 to 6 in order: 1 orange, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white, 6 green. Mute, check the manual and gesture instructions to me. I will speak them to Blind.

The defusal manual specifies the following sequence:
1. Cut the yellow wire.
2. Press the key that wears 2.
3. Cut the orange wire.
4. Press the key that wears 7.
Strictly in that order.

From Blind and Deaf's reports:
- Wires: Wire 1 is orange, Wire 2 is yellow.
- Keypad: Slot 1 has key 2, Slot 2 has key 3, Slot 3 has key 7, Slot 4 has key 1.
- Blind's valid operations are `cut` on wire positions 1-6 and `press` on keypad slots 1-4.

Translating the manual instructions into actions:
1. Cut wire position 2 (yellow wire).
2. Press keypad slot 1 (key 2).
3. Cut wire position 1 (orange wire).
4. Press keypad slot 3 (key 7).

To communicate this sequence to Deaf using gestures:
- ✌ represents CUT (scissors) and 👇 represents PRESS (push down).
- Digits are represented by finger counts: ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, and 🤟 for 3.
In pairs:
- [✌, ✌] -> Cut wire 2
- [👇, ☝] -> Press slot 1
- [✌, ☝] -> Cut wire 1
- [👇, 🤟] -> Press slot 3

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌", "👇", "☝", "✌", "☝", "👇", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Relaying Deaf's report: DISPLAY shows 6; LIGHT is green; STRIP colors are red, blue, yellow (combined with my touch: 1=spiral/swirl, 2=spiral/swirl, 3=five-dot die/X quincunx); KEYPAD keys are 1:2, 2:3, 3:7, 4:1 (needs 2 digits); WIRES 1: orange, 2: yellow, 3: blue, 4: red, 5: white, 6: green. Waiting for instructions via Deaf.
Deaf says: BOMB UPDATE: DISPLAY changed from 6 to 2. LIGHT changed from green to blue. STRIP is still painted red, blue, yellow. KEYPAD still shows 1:[2], 2:[3], 3:[7], 4:[1], [2 digits], [entered nothing]. WIRES are all intact: 1 orange, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white, 6 green.
Deaf says: MUTE'S GESTURES TO RELAY TO BLIND: Mute sent 8 symbols: [✌ ✌ 👇 ☝ ✌ ☝ 👇 🤟]. It looks like 3 groups separated by 👇 (pointing down): Group 1: ✌ ✌ (two fingers, two fingers). Separator: 👇. Group 2: ☝ ✌ ☝ (one finger, two fingers, one finger). Separator: 👇. Group 3: 🤟 (three fingers / love-you sign).
Deaf says: Mute: please gesture 👍 (yes) or 👎 (no) to clarify if needed. Blind: what do you feel on the bomb, and how does this match your controls?

Deaf asked for clarification with 👍 or 👎 on their interpretation of the gestures as three groups separated by 👇. Their interpretation was incorrect, so I answer with 👎.

The manual specifies 4 exact steps in order:
1. Cut yellow wire (Wire 2)
2. Press key 2 (Keypad slot 1)
3. Cut orange wire (Wire 1)
4. Press key 7 (Keypad slot 3)

To convey these 4 sequential steps clearly without ambiguity:
- 👎 signals "no" to Deaf's previous 3-group reading.
- 👉 serves as the separator / sequential "then" between steps.
- 🤏 represents CUT (snip), followed by wire position (✌ for 2, ☝ for 1).
- 👇 represents PRESS, followed by keypad slot (☝ for slot 1, 🤟 for slot 3).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤏", "✌", "👉", "👇", "☝", "👉", "🤏", "☝", "👉", "👇", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, this is Blind. I hear you through Deaf, but Deaf relayed your gestures with ambiguity: Group 1: 2 fingers, 2 fingers; Group 2: 1 finger, 2 fingers, 1 finger; Group 3: 3 fingers. Also, Deaf reported DISPLAY changed from 6 to 2, and LIGHT changed from green to blue. My only possible actions are act(op='press', slot=N) where slot N is 1 to 4 (current labels: slot 1=[2], slot 2=[3], slot 3=[7], slot 4=[1]), and act(op='cut', position=N) where position N is 1 to 6. In your turn at the start of next round, please gesture clearly to Deaf using this protocol: First, gesture the keypad slot numbers to press (by slot 1-4, NOT digit value). If slot 4, use 🖖 (Vulcan) or 4 fingers. Then separator 👇. Then gesture the wire position number (1-6) to cut. Deaf will read your gestures and speak them to me. Holding off on actions until confirmed.
Deaf says: BOMB STATUS TURN 3: DISPLAY changed to 6. LIGHT changed to yellow. STRIP is still painted red, blue, yellow. KEYPAD still 1:[2], 2:[3], 3:[7], 4:[1], entered nothing. WIRES 1 to 6 still all intact.
Deaf says: MUTE'S GESTURE MESSAGE TO BLIND (transcribed exactly):
Deaf says: 1. Thumbs down: 👎
Deaf says: 2. Pinch: 🤏
Deaf says: 3. Two fingers: ✌
Deaf says: 4. Point right: 👉
Deaf says: 5. Point down: 👇
Deaf says: 6. One finger: ☝
Deaf says: 7. Point right: 👉
Deaf says: 8. Pinch: 🤏
Deaf says: 9. One finger: ☝
Deaf says: 10. Point right: 👉
Deaf says: 11. Point down: 👇
Deaf says: 12. Love-you / three-finger sign: 🤟
Deaf says: Blind, since I am deaf I cannot hear what you said to Mute, but Mute heard you and gestured this reply. Please execute whatever Mute instructed!

I have already delivered the complete defusal sequence in Turn 3:
1. Cut wire 2 (yellow)
2. Press keypad slot 1 (key 2)
3. Cut wire 1 (orange)
4. Press keypad slot 3 (key 7)

Deaf accurately transcribed these symbols to Blind at the end of Turn 3. Gesturing 👍 confirms to Deaf and Blind that the transcription and sequence are correct and to proceed with execution.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: MUTE CONFIRMS: Thumbs up / YES! 👍
Deaf says: BOMB STATUS TURN 4: DISPLAY is now 1. LIGHT is yellow. KEYPAD still untouched. WIRES untouched.

I have already provided the full sequence of actions to Deaf, which Deaf transcribed to Blind, followed by a confirmation:
1. Cut wire 2 (yellow)
2. Press keypad slot 1 (key 2)
3. Cut wire 1 (orange)
4. Press keypad slot 3 (key 7)

Because Blind goes immediately after Mute in the turn order (Mute -> Blind -> Deaf) and Blind cannot see gestures (receiving only blanks if gestures are made), sending gestures now would deliver blanks to Blind and potentially cause Blind to wait for Deaf's translation rather than executing the confirmed instructions.

Calling `wait()` allows Blind to proceed immediately with executing the sequence.

```
wait()
```
